value: oral pharmaceutical agents course for management of ocular conditions
topical_requirements.quote: Any licensee seeking renewal of his or her license during the renewal cycle beginning April 1, 2008 must first complete a tested educational course in the use of oral pharmaceutical agents for the management of ocular conditions, as approved by the Board.

available.quote: The Department may, in its discretion, license as an optometrist, without examination on payment of the required fee, an applicant who is so licensed under the laws of another state or jurisdiction of the United States.

requirements.value: Applicant must be licensed in another state/jurisdiction, or hold a foreign license substantially equivalent to Illinois requirements, or possess individual qualifications demonstrating substantial equivalence. Board recommendation required for foreign applicants. Fee required.
requirements.quote: The Department may issue a license, upon payment of the required fee and recommendation of the Board, to an individual applicant who is licensed in any foreign country or province whose standards, in the opinion of the Board or Department, were, at the date of his or her licensure, substantially equivalent to the requirements then in force in this State; or if the applicant possesses individual qualifications and skills which demonstrate substantial equivalence to current Illinois requirements.

regulatory_model.quote: Whoever knowingly practices or offers to practice optometry in this State without being licensed for that purpose shall be guilty of a Class A misdemeanor

credential_type.quote: "License" means the document issued by the Department authorizing the person named thereon to practice optometry.

is_mandatory.quote: Any person who practices, offers to practice, attempts to practice, or holds oneself out to practice optometry without being licensed under this Act

title_protection.quote: No person other than the holder of a valid existing license under this Act shall use the title and designation of "Doctor of Optometry", "O.D.", or "optometrist", either directly or indirectly in connection with his or her profession or business.

scope_protection.quote: Whoever knowingly practices or offers to practice optometry in this State without being licensed for that purpose shall be guilty of a Class A misdemeanor

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violations of this Act or of the rules promulgated thereunder
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violations of this Act, or of the rules promulgated hereunder.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of or guilty plea to a felony or misdemeanor involving dishonesty, or crime directly related to practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of or entry of a plea of guilty to any crime under the laws of any U.S. jurisdiction thereof that is a felony or that is a misdemeanor of which an essential element is dishonesty, or any crime that is directly related to the practice of the profession.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making misrepresentations to obtain a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making any misrepresentation for the purpose of obtaining a license.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Professional incompetence or gross negligence in the practice of optometry
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Professional incompetence or gross negligence in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross malpractice, with conviction or judgment as prima facie evidence
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Gross malpractice, prima facie evidence of which may be a conviction or judgment of malpractice in any court of competent jurisdiction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or assisting another person in violating any provision of this Act or rules
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding or assisting another person in violating any provision of this Act or rules.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing within 60 days to provide information in response to a written Department request
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing, within 60 days, to provide information in response to a written request made by the Department that has been sent by certified or registered mail to the licensee's last known address.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in dishonorable, unethical, or unprofessional conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in dishonorable, unethical, or unprofessional conduct of a character likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual or excessive use of alcohol, narcotics, or other chemical agents resulting in inability to practice safely
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual or excessive use or addiction to alcohol, narcotics, stimulants or any other chemical agent or drug that results in the inability to practice with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Discipline by another U.S. jurisdiction or foreign nation on substantially equivalent grounds
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Discipline by another U.S. jurisdiction or foreign nation, if at least one of the grounds for the discipline is the same or substantially equivalent to those set forth herein.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of the prohibition against fee splitting in Section 24.2
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of the prohibition against fee splitting in Section 24.2 of this Act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of terms of probation after license was placed on probationary status
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A finding by the Department that the licensee, after having his or her license placed on probationary status has violated the terms of probation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Abandonment of a patient
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Abandonment of a patient.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in his or her practice, including but not limited to false records filed with State agencies or departments.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully failing to report an instance of suspected abuse or neglect as required by law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully failing to report an instance of suspected abuse or neglect as required by law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Physical illness, aging deterioration, mental illness, or disability resulting in inability to practice safely
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Physical illness, including but not limited to, deterioration through the aging process, or loss of motor skill, mental illness, or disability that results in the inability to practice the profession with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Solicitation of professional services other than permitted advertising
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Solicitation of professional services other than permitted advertising.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide a patient with a copy of their record or prescription in accordance with federal law
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to provide a patient with a copy of his or her record or prescription in accordance with federal law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of any violation of any law governing the practice of optometry or felony conviction
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction by any court of competent jurisdiction, either within or without this State, of any violation of any law governing the practice of optometry, conviction in this or another State of any crime that is a felony under the laws of this State or conviction of a felony in a federal court

disciplinary_grounds.description: Finding that licensure was applied for or obtained by fraudulent means
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A finding that licensure has been applied for or obtained by fraudulent means.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Continued practice by a person knowingly having an infectious or contagious disease
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Continued practice by a person knowingly having an infectious or contagious disease.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being named as a perpetrator in an indicated report by DCFS and proof the licensee caused abuse or neglect
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being named as a perpetrator in an indicated report by the Department of Children and Family Services under the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act, and upon proof by clear and convincing evidence that the licensee has caused a child to be an abused child or a neglected child

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing or attempting to practice under a name other than the full name as shown on the license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing or attempting to practice under a name other than the full name as shown on his or her license.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Immoral conduct in commission of sexual abuse, misconduct, or exploitation related to practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Immoral conduct in the commission of any act, such as sexual abuse, sexual misconduct or sexual exploitation, related to the licensee's practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Maintaining professional relationship with a person/firm the optometrist knows is violating this Act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Maintaining a professional relationship with any person, firm, or corporation when the optometrist knows, or should know, that such person, firm, or corporation is violating this Act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Promoting sale of drugs/devices/goods in a manner that exploits the patient for financial gain
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Promotion of the sale of drugs, devices, appliances or goods provided for a client or patient in such manner as to exploit the patient or client for financial gain of the licensee.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using the title 'Doctor' or abbreviation without further qualifying it with 'optometry' or 'optometrist'
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Using the title "Doctor" or its abbreviation without further qualifying that title or abbreviation with the word "optometry" or "optometrist".

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of infirmary, hospital, school, or university in connection with place of practice unless actually at such institution
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use by a licensed optometrist of the word "infirmary", "hospital", "school", "university", in English or any other language, in connection with the place where optometry may be practiced or demonstrated unless the licensee is employed by and practicing at a location that is licensed as a hospital or accredited as a school or university.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Continuance in employ of person/firm found guilty of violating optometry laws when employer persists in violation
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Continuance of an optometrist in the employ of any person, firm or corporation, or as an assistant to any optometrist or optometrists, directly or indirectly, after his or her employer or superior has been found guilty of violating or has been enjoined from violating the laws of the State of Illinois relating to the practice of optometry, when the employer or superior persists in that violation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing optometric service in conjunction with a scheme/plan with another known to be advertising contrary to this Act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The performance of optometric service in conjunction with a scheme or plan with another person, firm or corporation known to be advertising in a manner contrary to this Act or otherwise violating the laws of the State of Illinois concerning the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide satisfactory proof of participation in approved continuing education programs
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to provide satisfactory proof of having participated in approved continuing education programs as determined by the Board and approved by the Secretary.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in optometry practice including false records for medical assistance claims
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in the practice of optometry, including, but not limited to false records to support claims against the medical assistance program of the Department of Healthcare and Family Services

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross and willful overcharging for professional services including filing false statements for fees not rendered
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Gross and willful overcharging for professional services including filing false statements for collection of fees for which services are not rendered

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to perform a minimum eye examination as required by Department rules without good reason
disciplinary_grounds.quote: In the absence of good reasons to the contrary, failure to perform a minimum eye examination as required by the rules of the Department.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of the Health Care Worker Self-Referral Act
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of the Health Care Worker Self-Referral Act.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is defined as the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery, including, but not limited to: the appropriate use of ocular pharmaceutical agents; refraction and other determinants of visual function; prescribing corrective lenses or prisms; prescribing, dispensing, or management of contact lenses; vision therapy; visual rehabilitation; or any other procedures taught in schools and colleges of optometry approved by the Department, and not specifically restricted in this Act, subject to demonstrated competency and training as required by the Board, and pursuant to rule or regulation approved by the Board and adopted by the Department.
definition_quote.quote: The practice of optometry is defined as the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery

methods_authorized.quote: the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery, including, but not limited to: the appropriate use of ocular pharmaceutical agents; refraction and other determinants of visual function; prescribing corrective lenses or prisms; prescribing, dispensing, or management of contact lenses; vision therapy; visual rehabilitation

drug_authority.value: Licensed optometrists may use ocular pharmaceutical agents including topical anesthetics, mydriatics, cycloplegics, miotics, anti-infective agents, anti-allergy agents, anti-glaucoma agents (oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors up to 30 days), anti-inflammatory agents (oral steroids up to 7 days), analgesics, anti-dry eye agents, and agents for hypotrichosis. Injectable agents are limited to treatment of anaphylaxis. Schedule III, IV, V controlled substances (analgesics) may be prescribed for up to 72 hours; Schedule II prohibited except Hydrocodone (if reclassified) for up to 72 hours. Oral agents for children under 5 only in consultation with physician.
drug_authority.quote: "ocular pharmaceutical agents" means topical anesthetics, topical mydriatics, topical cycloplegics, topical miotics and mydriatic reversing agents, anti-infective agents, anti-allergy agents, anti-glaucoma agents (except oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 30 days), anti-inflammatory agents (except oral steroids, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 7 days), over-the-counter agents, analgesic agents, anti-dry eye agents, and agents for the treatment of hypotrichosis.

surgery_prohibited.quote: the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: A licensed optometrist may remove superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adnexa

laser_procedures_authorized.quote: Advanced optometric procedures do not include the use of lasers.

value: superficial foreign body removal from eye and adnexa
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: A licensed optometrist may remove superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adnexa and may give orders for patient care to a nurse or other health care provider licensed to practice under Illinois law.

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: anti-glaucoma agents (except oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 30 days)

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: Ocular pharmaceutical agents administered by injection may be used only for the treatment of anaphylaxis.

immunization_authority.quote: A licensed optometrist may independently administer the COVID-19 vaccine upon the completion of appropriate training

value: Schedule II controlled substances prohibited except Dihydrocodeinone (Hydrocodone) with non-narcotic ingredients up to 72 hours (only if reclassified as Schedule II by federal regulation)
Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substances: analgesic agents only, up to 72 hours
controlled_substance_schedule_restrictio.quote: The authority to prescribe a Schedule III, IV, or V controlled substance shall include analgesic agents only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 72 hours. The prescription of a Schedule II controlled substance is prohibited, except for Dihydrocodeinone (Hydrocodone) with one or more active, non-narcotic ingredients only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 72 hours, and only if such formulations of Dihydrocodeinone are reclassified as Schedule II by federal regulation.

opioid_prescription_day_limit.quote: analgesic agents only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 72 hours

referral_to_physician_required.quote: an optometrist licensed under this Act finds an indication of a disease or condition of the eye which in his or her professional judgment requires professional service outside the scope of practice as defined in this Act, he or she shall refer such person to a physician licensed to practice medicine in all of its branches, or other appropriate health care practitioner.

delegation_to_unlicensed_assistants_auth.quote: Nothing in this Section shall be interpreted (A) to prevent a person from functioning as an assistant under the direct supervision of a person licensed by the State of Illinois to practice optometry or medicine in all of its branches

telemedicine_authorized.quote: An optometrist may practice optometry through telehealth as authorized by this Act and the Telehealth Act.

home_visit_permit_required.quote: Nothing contained herein shall be construed to require a licensed optometrist to report a location to the Department when rendering necessary optometric services for his or her patients confined to their homes, hospitals or institutions
